resource.name: Environment_NYC
resource.description: Street tree records from the 2015 TreesCount! census run by NYC Parks and partners. Fields include species, diameter, and perceived health. Collection ran from May 2015 to October 2016 and covers trees along city streets under Parks jurisdiction; the dataset is a point-in-time snapshot. The census data supports the agency's forestry inventory and management.
columns_description: Indicates the user's perception of tree health.
Unique identification number for each tree point.
Diameter of the tree, measured at approximately 54" / 137cm above the ground. Data was collected for both living and dead trees; for stumps, use stump_diam
Indicates whether the tree is alive, standing dead, or a stump.
Indicates the presence of a root problem caused by paving stones in tree bed
The species of the tree, which can influence health due to varying resilience to environmental factors.
Type of location where the tree is planted (e.g., residential, commercial, park).
An estimate of the soil quality around the tree (e.g., poor, average, good).
Average annual precipitation in the area where the tree is located.
Average annual temperature in the area where the tree is located.
Density of urban development in the vicinity of the tree.
Estimated age of the tree based on its diameter and species growth rates.
Indicator of pest infestation in the area (e.g., low, medium, high).
History of diseases affecting trees in the area.
How often the tree is maintained (e.g., regularly, occasionally, rarely).
Distance from the tree to known pollution sources (e.g., roads, factories).
Accessibility of water sources for the tree (e.g., easy, moderate, difficult).
Amount of sunlight the tree receives daily (e.g., full, partial, low).
Availability of space for tree roots to grow (e.g., limited, adequate, abundant).
